key_insight: Introduce global scene tokens that provide holistic scene awareness to a feed‑forward Gaussian splatting pipeline, enabling efficient, compact allocation of 3D primitives that preserves high-fidelity reconstruction while remaining fast to infer.
problem_solved: Overcomes the limitations of local, heuristic-driven allocation in 3D Gaussian Splatting that force a trade-off between representation compactness, reconstruction quality, and feed‑forward inference speed.
method: Learn a small set of global scene tokens that summarize global geometry and appearance, used to guide allocation and parameterization of 3D Gaussian primitives.
Use a feed‑forward network (global-token conditioning + local decoding) to predict Gaussian positions, covariances, colors and confidences in one pass, replacing iterative optimization.
Train with reconstruction loss plus regularizers for sparsity/compactness so the model balances fidelity, size, and render speed.
impact: Delivers a practical route to real‑time, high‑quality neural rendering with far fewer primitives and predictable inference latency, making 3D Gaussian Splatting more usable in production pipelines and interactive applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: global scene tokens extracted from input images → token-conditioned decoder → resulting 3D Gaussians → fast rasterized render
Before/after comparison: local-heuristic allocation vs GlobalSplat showing fewer Gaussians with equal or better visual fidelity
Attention/token map overlay: visualization of how global tokens attend to different scene regions guiding allocation
Performance chart: trade-off plot of reconstruction quality vs number of primitives and inference time comparing prior methods and GlobalSplat
paper_title: GlobalSplat: Efficient Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting via Global Scene Tokens
paper_authors: Roni Itkin, Noam Issachar, Yehonatan Keypur, Yehonatan Keypur, Anpei Chen
